text:
dmitri: Heads-up — I found a correctness regression after enabling activation quantization + FP8 matmul in nightly. Small model, deterministic seed, outputs diverge vs FP16 baseline.

maria: Ugh, when did this land? Did we flip any kernel selection logic recently? @alex any recent triton kernel touches?

alex: I merged the FP8 kernel selection switch last week (opt-in flag). It picks fp8_fast_matmul if seq_len <= 128 and batch <= 16. No code path changes to cache handling AFAIK.

sophie: Can you paste a minimal repro?

dmitri: Repro below (really small).

```
# repro
python tools/repro_fp8.py --model tiny --seq 64 --batch 8 --seed 42 --use-fp8-activations
# observed
Token 12: ref=0.234567 -> fp8=0.130122 (diff > 1e-2)
```

aj: Quick question — is KV cache enabled in that run? We saw earlier cache indexing quirks with mixed precision.

dmitri: Good call — repro used cached decoding path (streaming). If I disable KV reuse and recompute from scratch, outputs match FP16.

maria: So bug surfaces only when reusing KV cache + FP8 activation quant? That narrows it a lot. Maybe quantization state not reset between incremental batches.

alex: I ran nvprof on the failing run. Kernel chosen: fp8_matmul_fast (time 1.85ms), fallback fp16 would be ~2.05ms. Perf looks fine but correctness broken. nvprof snippet:

```
== Profiling result ==
fp8_matmul_fast     1.850ms   0.0000s   8.3GB/s
kv_cache_read       0.120ms
other               0.900ms
```

sophie: Does the bug reproduce with batch=1? Dmitri said batch=8.

dmitri: I tested batch=1 streaming + kv reuse -> works. Batch>1 triggers divergence. Also if I force kernel to fp16 path, divergence disappears even with batch>1.

aj: Hypothesis: mixed-precision accumulator or quant scale is shared incorrectly across items in a batch when using streaming updates. Maybe scale vector not broadcast correctly for mixed batch dims.

maria: Could be an indexing bug in the matmul wrapper that uses cumulative kv_offset. For FP8 we have per-column scaling metadata; if kv_offset isn't applied the scales mis-align.

alex: I added debug prints inside kernel selection wrapper. For batch=8 we pass scale_ptr pointing to offset 0 for all rows — looks like we overwrite the per-batch scale buffer in-place during incremental update.

sophie: Any stack traces or checksums? A quick binary diff on last-layer activations shows systematic attenuation on a specific head. That smells like wrong accumulator dtype or wrong cast (FP8->FP16) order.

```
# debug dump
layer_7_head_3_act_fp16_checksum: 0x7a1f2b
layer_7_head_3_act_fp8_run_checksum: 0x4d0c9a
```

aj: Also saw this in profiler: when KV reuse path is taken, we emit an extra memcpy that for FP8 we annotated as in-place. Could be a race where we quantize the wrong buffer.

maria: Can we reproduce inside python (no GPU concurrency) with deterministic single stream? If it's an in-place mutation bug it should still show up.

dmitri: Repro attached: tools/repro_fp8_minimal.py uses a single CUDA stream and syncs. Still fails.

alex: I bisected to the change that added "activation_quant.write_back = true" optimization (commit 2f8b). Reverting that makes the issue go away. Looks like write_back reuses target buffer pointer across batch slots.

sophie: That matches: write_back was an in-place optimization to avoid extra allocs for quantized activations. If pointer arithmetic is wrong for batched KV offsets you get misaligned scales.

aj: Proposed fix: stop doing in-place write_back for FP8 when kv_reuse==true OR ensure we compute per-batch offsets correctly and do a safe memcpy. Short-term: revert the optimization or gate it behind a flag.

maria: Agreed. Also add a unit test that toggles kv_reuse + batch>1 + fp8 path and compares to fp16 baseline (checksum equality within tolerance).

alex: I'll put up a PR that disables write_back for FP8+kv_reuse and adds test + reproducer. Marking as rollback candidate for nightly.

ops-bot: deploy-notify: nightly inference images flagged for rollback due to failing correctness test #invocations=3 status=non-zero

dmitri: Thanks. After hotfix we should also run a small sweep for calibration side-effects: FP8 calibration (per-tensor vs per-channel) may interact with incremental KV quantization states. Calibration mismatch could hide or exacerbate this.

sophie: Good point — add calibration-mode matrix in tests (per-tensor/per-channel) and check outputs.

maria: Follow-ups: 1) PR to gate write_back (alex) 2) Add regression test + calibration combos (maria+aj) 3) Run dedicated perf check to ensure we don't regress latency beyond ~5% (sophie).

aj: I'll also look at kernel select heuristics. If FP8 path gives incorrect results in any path with kv_reuse we should prevent it from being autopicked until the bug is fixed. Better safe than fast.

alex: Working on PR now, will link in thread. ETA ~2 hrs.

dmitri: Great, thx. Leaving the repro and logs in /tmp/fp8_repro_1718001234.tar.gz.

maria: tagging eng-ml for visibility. @sre FYI in case we need a hot rollback on Dedicated clusters. :rotating_light:
